initial_requirements: European card-issuing authorities need a shared TACHOnet service to coordinate driver smart-card requests across participating member organizations. Users should be able to ask one or more members about the possible delivery or status of cards, receive standardized replies, and follow each request through completion. The service should also manage access rights, alert participants when expected replies are late, and provide operational statistics.

turns.interviewer_utterance: What are the primary business objectives and success criteria for the shared TACHOnet service, and which outcomes are most important to achieve first?
turns.interviewee_utterance:
The main business objective is to give participating card-issuing authorities a reliable shared coordination service so they can check card request status across borders without each organization having to chase others separately. Success means requests are answered in a standardized way, status is visible through to completion, access is controlled properly, and overdue replies are flagged so cases do not stall.
What matters most first is making the core request-and-reply flow work consistently, because that is the operational heart of the service. After that, the priority is tracking deadlines and late responses, then access management, and finally the reporting and statistics so the organizations can monitor how well the network is performing.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Which stakeholder roles or participating organizations will use, operate, administer, or receive outputs from the TACHOnet service, and what responsibilities does each role have?
turns.interviewee_utterance: The main users are the European card-issuing authorities that participate in the network, since they will send requests and receive standardized replies about card delivery or status. There will also be operational administrators for the shared service who manage access rights, monitor overdue replies, and keep the coordination service running smoothly. On top of that, management or oversight users may receive the operational statistics and status reports, but I’m not sure yet whether those are separate people or part of the same organizations’ back-office teams.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Beyond the core request-and-reply flow, deadline tracking, access control, and reporting, what specific functions should the TACHOnet service provide from end to end—for example, request submission, routing to one or more member organizations, reply tracking, notifications, case follow-up, and completion handling?
turns.interviewee_utterance: End to end, I’d expect it to let a user create and submit a request, send it to one or more selected member organizations, and then track each individual reply against that case. It should notify the sender when replies arrive or when a response is late, and keep the case open until all expected answers are back or the requester closes it. Once finished, it should store the outcome so the full history can be reviewed later.

turns.interviewer_utterance: When a request needs to be sent to one or more member organizations, how should the service determine which members to route it to, and are there any rules for sequencing, parallel delivery, retries, or excluding certain members?
turns.interviewee_utterance: The service should route based on the member or members the requester selects, using the network’s authorized participant list rather than trying to infer the target automatically. My understanding is that delivery to multiple members would usually be in parallel, because the goal is to get responses efficiently, but I’d need to confirm whether any cases require a sequence instead. I don’t know the exact retry or exclusion rules yet, though I would expect the service to avoid sending to members that are not currently active or not authorized for that type of request.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Could you define the full request lifecycle and the rules for standardized replies—for example, what status states a request should move through from submission to completion, what each member’s reply must contain or how it should be formatted, and exactly what conditions allow a case to be closed?
turns.interviewee_utterance: A request would normally move from submitted to sent, then to awaiting reply, and then to completed once all expected responses are in, or to closed if it is cancelled or otherwise terminated. Each reply should come back in a standardized format so the requesting authority can reliably read the status, the result, and any supporting message or reference data; the exact fields would need to follow the TACHOnet message definition, which I don’t have in front of me. A case can be closed when all required replies have been received, or if the requester decides no further follow-up is needed, but I’d want to verify whether there are any mandatory waiting periods before closure.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Before a requester is allowed to close a case early, are there any mandatory waiting periods or minimum time windows that must elapse, and if so what are the exact rules for when closure is permitted or blocked?
turns.interviewee_utterance: I don’t have the exact waiting-period rules confirmed yet, so I can’t state a fixed minimum time window with confidence. My expectation is that closure would be blocked while any required reply is still within its allowed response deadline, and only permitted once the requester has either received all expected responses or is explicitly allowed to abandon the case. If there are mandatory grace periods or legal retention windows, those would need to be checked with the business owners or the message specification.

turns.interviewer_utterance: Can you define the standardized TACHOnet reply message structure in more detail—what fields are required versus optional, what each field should represent, and whether there are any specific validation, code-set, or reference-data rules we need to follow?
turns.interviewee_utterance: I can’t define the exact TACHOnet reply structure from memory, because that has to match the formal interface specification and code lists used by the network. In general, I would expect required fields for the case or request identifier, the responding member, the response status, the timestamp, and any result or reason code, with optional free-text comments or supporting references. The validation rules should enforce the agreed code sets and formats very strictly so every member can process replies consistently, but I’d need to verify the exact field names and allowed values against the standard.

slots.name: project_goals
slots.value: Provide participating card-issuing authorities with a reliable shared coordination service for cross-border card request status checks; ensure standardized replies, end-to-end request visibility, proper access control, and alerts for overdue responses. Highest priority is the core request-and-reply flow, followed by deadline/late-response tracking, access management, and then reporting/statistics.

slots.name: stakeholder_roles
slots.value: Primary users are European card-issuing authorities participating in the network, which send requests and receive standardized replies about card delivery or status. Operational administrators manage access rights, monitor overdue replies, and keep the coordination service running. Management or oversight users may receive operational statistics and status reports, but it is unclear whether they are separate roles or part of the organizations' back-office teams.

slots.name: functional_needs
slots.value: The service should let users create and submit requests, route each request to one or more selected member organizations, track individual replies against the case, notify the sender when replies arrive or are late, keep the case open until all expected answers are received or the requester closes it, and store completed outcomes for later review.

slots.name: data_entities
slots.value: Core data elements include a request/case identifier, the responding member organization, reply status, timestamp, result or reason code, and possibly free-text comments or supporting references. Requests and replies must remain linked to the originating case.

slots.name: constraints
slots.value: Replies and message content must conform to the formal TACHOnet interface specification and agreed code lists/formats. Routing should use the network's authorized participant list and avoid inactive or unauthorized members. Mandatory grace periods and legal retention windows are not yet confirmed.

slots.name: quality_concerns
slots.value: The service must be reliable and consistent, with standardized responses and controlled access. It should support timely follow-up by flagging overdue replies so requests do not stall.

slots.name: boundary_conditions
slots.value: Exact retry behavior, exclusion rules, mandatory waiting periods, and legal retention windows are not yet defined and need confirmation with the business owners or message specification.

slots.name: request_lifecycle_states
slots.value: A request normally moves from submitted to sent to awaiting reply, then to completed once all expected responses are received, or to closed if it is cancelled or otherwise terminated.

slots.name: reply_standardization_rules
slots.value: Replies must use the formal TACHOnet message specification and agreed code lists/validation rules. At minimum, the reply should include the case or request identifier, responding member, response status, timestamp, and a result or reason code, with optional comments or supporting references.

slots.name: deadline_management_policy
slots.value: Late replies should be flagged when a response is overdue; closure should be blocked while any required reply is still within its allowed response deadline, and only permitted once all expected responses are received or the requester is explicitly allowed to abandon the case. Any mandatory grace periods or legal retention windows are not yet confirmed.

slots.name: audit_and_traceability_requirements
slots.value: The full request history should remain linked through completion, and completed outcomes should be stored for later review. Audit detail beyond traceability is not yet specified.

slots.name: reporting_and_statistics_scope
slots.value: Operational statistics and status reports should be available for management or oversight users to monitor how well the network is performing.

slots.name: multi_recipient_routing_rules
slots.value: Requests are routed based on the member or members selected by the requester, using the network’s authorized participant list rather than automatic target inference. Delivery to multiple members is usually parallel for efficiency; exact sequencing rules are not yet confirmed. The service should avoid sending requests to members that are not currently active or not authorized for that request type.

slots.name: case_closure_criteria
slots.value: A case can be closed when all required replies have been received, or if the requester decides no further follow-up is needed; it is not yet confirmed whether any mandatory waiting periods apply before closure.

slots.name: requester_control_over_followup
slots.value: The requester can decide no further follow-up is needed and close the case before all responses are received, subject to any blocking deadline rules.

slots.name: response_correlation_and_case_linking
slots.value: Each individual reply is tracked against the originating case so the full request history remains linked through completion.

slots.name: closure_waiting_period_rules
slots.value: No fixed minimum time window is confirmed yet; closure is expected to be blocked while any required reply is still within its allowed response deadline. Possible grace periods or legal retention windows remain to be verified.

slots.name: message_schema_and_required_fields
slots.value: Expected reply fields include the case or request identifier, responding member, response status, timestamp, result or reason code, and optional free-text comments or supporting references. Exact field names, allowed values, and validation rules must follow the formal TACHOnet specification.

slots.name: retention_and_archival_policy
slots.value: Completed outcomes should be stored for later review, but the exact retention and archival rules are not yet defined.

slots.name: notification_rules_for_reply_and_deadline_events
slots.value: The system should notify the sender when replies arrive and when responses are late; overdue replies should also be flagged for operational monitoring.
